NDT training in Winnipeg: how it works for Winnipeg employers and technicians

Short answer: Atlantis NDT delivers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I, II and III training in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET for Manitoba employers and technicians. We teach it live online or onsite at your shop, hangar or plant, under ASNT Level III oversight. We have no classroom in Winnipeg. Canada's national scheme is still CAN/CGSB-48.9712, certified by NRCan's NDTCB. Our training suits Winnipeg firms that work to US codes or for US clients, including work in North Dakota and Minnesota.

Winnipeg's NDT market isn't built on refineries, the way Sarnia's or Edmonton's is. It rests on four other areas: aerospace manufacturing and engine overhaul, heavy vehicle and rail manufacturing, hydroelectric generation, and the pipeline corridors that cross southern Manitoba toward the US border. Each has its own certification expectations:

  • Canadian industrial and pipeline owners generally expect certification from Natural Resources Canada's National Non-Destructive Testing Certification Body (NRCan NDTCB) under CAN/CGSB-48.9712. That standard is the Canadian adoption of ISO 9712, and the certificate belongs to the technician.
  • Aerospace employers usually qualify NDT personnel to aerospace-specific standards such as NAS 410 or EN 4179, under their customers' and Nadcap requirements.
  • US clients from Grand Forks and Fargo down through the Twin Cities, and the US parent companies of several Winnipeg manufacturers, mostly work to ASNT SNT-TC-1A. That is an employer-based scheme: the company's written practice governs, and a Level III examines and certifies each technician.

Atlantis NDT trains to SNT-TC-1A. We don't claim CGSB or NDTCB recognition, and we don't train to NAS 410. Our courses fit Winnipeg well in these cases:

  • Industrial firms with US work. Manitoba fabricators, inspection contractors and manufacturers whose US customers or US-code contracts call for SNT-TC-1A-qualified personnel.
  • Companies needing an outside Level III. Firms that need someone to write and run an SNT-TC-1A programme because they don't employ a full-time Level III.
  • Method theory for any scheme. UT, ET or PT physics and technique are the same under every scheme. Check your target scheme's own hour-credit and exam rules first.

If that describes you, request a Winnipeg training quote. Include the methods, levels, head count and whether you want online or onsite delivery.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Winnipeg

All courses follow the SNT-TC-1A body of knowledge and can be delivered to Winnipeg groups live online or onsite at the employer's facility. The employer's written practice sets the exact hours, experience and exam content. For reference figures, see the NDT training requirements matrix.

MethodLevelsWhat Winnipeg employers use it forPrerequisite
Ultrasonic Testing (UT)I, II, III prepWeld inspection on fabricated vessels and structures, rail wheel and axle inspection, thickness surveys on plant and pipeline assetsLevel I: basic maths and reading. Level II: Level I plus the experience your written practice requires
Phased Array UT (PAUT)II, III prepEncoded weld inspection on pipeline and plant piping, inspection of heavy fabrications and hydro componentsConventional UT, normally Level II
Time-of-Flight Diffraction (TOFD)II, III prepThick-section welds on penstocks, vessels and heavy fabrications, flaw height sizingConventional UT, normally Level II
Radiographic Testing (RT)I, II, III prepPipeline girth welds, pressure piping, castings and weldments in manufacturingRadiation safety training and CNSC operator credentials for gamma sources, in addition to method training
Magnetic Particle Testing (MT)I, II, III prepSurface cracks on bus and coach frames, rail components, agricultural equipment weldments, structural steelNone for Level I. Level II needs Level I plus experience
Liquid Penetrant Testing (PT)I, II, III prepNon-magnetic castings and forgings, stainless welds, aluminium structuresNone for Level I. Level II needs Level I plus experience
Visual Testing (VT)I, II, III prepWeld visual acceptance on structural and vehicle fabrication, hydro plant inspections, remote visual inspectionNone for Level I. Adequate near vision
Eddy Current Testing (ET)I, II, III prepSurface-crack detection on metallic components, tube inspection, conductivity and coating-thickness checksNone for Level I. Level II needs Level I plus experience

UT. The course runs from wave physics and calibration through angle-beam weld inspection, DAC and TCG, and evaluation against the relevant code. Winnipeg's job mix is broad. It spans structural and vehicle fabrication to CSA W59 or AWS D1.1, pressure equipment to ASME Section VIII, and rail components to railway specifications. We choose the specimens and code examples to match your work.

PAUT and TOFD. Cover focal laws, probe and wedge selection, scan planning, encoded capture and data analysis. TOFD adds diffraction theory and height sizing. These skills matter most on pipeline construction and integrity work, and on the thick sections found in hydroelectric plants.

RT. Covers radiation physics, exposure technique, film and digital imaging, image quality indicators, and weld and casting interpretation. The course does not give anyone the right to operate a gamma camera. See the licensing FAQ below.

MT, PT and VT. Manitoba's manufacturers depend heavily on these methods: bus and coach builders, agricultural-equipment makers and structural fabricators. Level II courses focus on technique selection, interpreting indications, and writing reports that satisfy both your quality system and your customer.

ET. Covers impedance-plane analysis, probes, reference standards, and surface-crack and tubing applications. For aerospace engine work, remember that the employer's aerospace qualification standard, usually NAS 410, sets the training and exam rules, not SNT-TC-1A.

If you are preparing for the ASNT Level III examinations, see our ASNT Level III training.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Winnipeg, step by step

The SNT-TC-1A route follows the same order in Winnipeg as anywhere else:

  1. The employer adopts a written practice. It defines training, experience, exams, vision tests, certification and recertification for each method and level. If you don't have one, see our written practice development service.
  2. Formal training. The technician completes the classroom hours the written practice requires, live online or onsite. The usual reference hours are in the training requirements matrix.
  3. On-the-job experience. Supervised, documented experience in the method, in your shop or on your projects.
  4. General examination. A written test on the principles of the method.
  5. Specific examination. A written test on your procedures, equipment and applicable codes and specifications.
  6. Practical examination. The technician inspects real specimens with known discontinuities, then documents and evaluates them. An NDT Level III administers or oversees the exam.
  7. Vision examination. Near-vision acuity each year, and colour contrast as specified in the written practice.
  8. Employer certification. The employer certifies the technician in writing and keeps the full record file.
  9. Recertification. At the interval the written practice sets. A new employer means certifying again under that employer's practice.

SNT-TC-1A certification stays with the employer, while NDTCB certification stays with the technician. The SNT-TC-1A training and certification guide explains the difference in more depth.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Winnipeg crews

Atlantis NDT has no training centre in Winnipeg or anywhere in Manitoba. We deliver in two ways:

  • Live online. Instructor-led theory taught in real time, with questions, worked examples and quizzes. This works well in Manitoba, where technicians may be spread from Winnipeg to Brandon, Selkirk, Steinbach and northern hydro sites, and where winter travel can be unpredictable. See NDT training online.
  • Onsite at your facility. An Atlantis instructor delivers training and practical sessions in your plant or shop, using your equipment and specimens that match your production: frame welds, castings, plate and pipe, or components. For multi-method or multi-site programmes, see corporate NDT training.

Scheduling around your work. Winnipeg's peaks come from production schedules, pipeline construction seasons, and planned outages at generating stations, rather than refinery turnarounds. Pipeline and field work often rushes in the warmer months, so many employers prefer to train over the winter and have certified people ready when field season opens. We build the calendar around that. Tell us your dates and we will send a cohort or onsite quote within one business day.

To get started, ask about onsite training for your Winnipeg crew.

Where NDT technicians work in Winnipeg

Winnipeg's inspection work is spread across these sectors:

  • Aerospace. Winnipeg is one of Canada's major aerospace centres. It has composite aerostructure manufacturing, gas-turbine engine repair and overhaul, and other aerospace manufacturers. The Royal Canadian Air Force's 17 Wing is also in the city. Aerospace NDT relies on UT for composites, and on ET, PT and borescope inspection of engine parts. It is qualified under NAS 410, EN 4179 and Nadcap. Atlantis doesn't train to those standards, so aerospace candidates should follow their employer's aerospace programme.
  • Bus, coach and heavy vehicle manufacturing. Winnipeg builds transit buses and motor coaches for customers across North America, many of them in the US. Frame and structural welds call for MT, PT, VT and UT. Because the buyers are American, SNT-TC-1A-qualified personnel are often useful here.
  • Rail. Major railway repair shops in Transcona and Weston, plus rail-car and component work across the region. Wheels, axles, couplers and welded structures are inspected with UT and MT.
  • Agricultural and industrial equipment. Manitoba makes combines, headers, tractors and grain-handling equipment. Structural and welding quality control calls for VT, MT and UT.
  • Hydroelectric power. Most of Manitoba's electricity comes from hydroelectric stations. The Winnipeg River plants are near the city, and the large Nelson River plants are in the north. Penstocks, turbine runners, gates, and generator and structural components are inspected with UT, PAUT, TOFD, MT and VT during planned outages.
  • Pipelines. Major crude and natural gas transmission lines cross southern Manitoba. They include Enbridge's Mainline, which runs toward the US border at Gretna, and TC Energy's Canadian Mainline. Federally regulated pipelines fall under the Canada Energy Regulator, and construction and integrity work generally follows CSA Z662. In the US, that work follows API 1104.
  • North Dakota and Minnesota. Grand Forks and Fargo are a short drive down I-29. The Bakken oilfield, midstream facilities, power plants and fabricators further south mostly work to SNT-TC-1A.

Codes you will meet locally. Boilers and pressure vessels in Manitoba are regulated under the province's boiler and pressure vessel legislation, which adopts CSA B51 and in turn references ASME Sections I, V and VIII and B31.1 and B31.3. Structural steel works to CSA W59, and welding fabricators are certified by the Canadian Welding Bureau under CSA W47.1. Pipelines use CSA Z662. For US customers you will meet AWS D1.1, API 1104 and ASME. Railway components follow railway-industry specifications.

Radiography licensing. The Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission (CNSC) licenses companies that possess and use gamma exposure devices, and certifies individual exposure device operators. Industrial X-ray equipment is regulated through Manitoba's workplace safety and health framework. In North Dakota and Minnesota, both NRC Agreement States, state radiation programmes license radioactive-materials radiography, and industrial radiographers need certification in line with the 10 CFR Part 34 framework. RT method training is needed as well as these credentials, not instead of them.

What Winnipeg employers typically ask for. Canadian industrial and pipeline owners: NRCan NDTCB certification to CAN/CGSB-48.9712. Aerospace: the employer's NAS 410 or EN 4179 qualification. US customers and US-code contracts: SNT-TC-1A certification backed by an auditable written practice. A mid-sized Winnipeg manufacturer can easily need two of these at once.

Level III services and written practices for Winnipeg NDT companies

Few Winnipeg manufacturers and inspection firms need a full-time Level III, but many need Level III work done properly. The most common case is a Manitoba manufacturer or contractor with US customers who has been asked for an SNT-TC-1A written practice and certified personnel. The job then needs:

  • A written practice that covers the methods and levels you use, aligned with the current SNT-TC-1A edition and your customers' requirements. Our written practice development service builds it around your operation.
  • Outside Level III services. Exam administration and grading, review of experience records, and certification sign-off under your written practice.
  • NDT procedures and technique sheets that match the customer's code, for example AWS D1.1 for vehicle frames or ASME Section V for pressure parts.
  • Customer-audit preparation. A review of certification files, vision records and training logs before a US customer's supplier audit.
  • Guidance on crediting existing training and experience, including history earned under NDTCB. We give it as guidance, not a promise of equivalence. Your written practice and your customer decide what counts.

For employer duties in plain language, see the SNT-TC-1A certification guide. If you would rather talk it through, book a Level III consultation for your Winnipeg company.

Practise before the practical exam

Atlantis offers Practical NDT, a 3D simulator where trainees practise 12 NDT methods in 5 environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site, and a storage tank. For Winnipeg trainees, the welding workshop fits manufacturing and fabrication, the aircraft hangar fits aerospace familiarisation, and the oil and gas site suits pipeline work. It lets trainees:

  • rehearse calibration and scanning
  • recognise indications
  • practise the order of an inspection before exam day

The simulator is a practice tool only. It does not replace the SNT-TC-1A practical examination on real specimens under Level III oversight, and it doesn't count as documented on-the-job experience.

Your instructor

Atlantis NDT training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. He designs the course content, oversees live-online and onsite delivery, and provides Level III oversight of examinations under the employer's written practice. When your Winnipeg team trains with Atlantis, you work directly with the Level III responsible for your programme.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Winnipeg

How do I get NDT certified in Winnipeg?

It depends on the work. Most Canadian industrial and pipeline owners expect NRCan NDTCB certification to CAN/CGSB-48.9712, which you apply and test for through NRCan. Aerospace employers qualify staff under their own NAS 410 or EN 4179 programmes. For US-code or US-customer work, your employer certifies you under its SNT-TC-1A written practice after training, experience, exams and a vision test. Atlantis delivers the SNT-TC-1A route.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Winnipeg employers?

Yes, by employers with US customers or US-code contracts, and by most employers in North Dakota and Minnesota. Many Canadian owners require NDTCB certification instead or as well, and aerospace employers use NAS 410. Confirm the requirement with your employer or client first. Atlantis doesn't claim CGSB or NDTCB recognition.

Can I take NDT training online in Manitoba?

Yes. Theory is delivered live online by an instructor, so you can join from Winnipeg or anywhere in Manitoba. Practical training and exams need real equipment and specimens, and we run them onsite at your employer's facility. See NDT training online.

Is there an Atlantis NDT training centre in Winnipeg?

No. Atlantis has no physical training centre in Winnipeg or any other city. We teach live online and onsite at the employer's facility.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

Under SNT-TC-1A, your employer's written practice sets it. It combines classroom hours for Level I and II with a required amount of documented on-the-job experience, and the experience normally takes the longest. See the reference figures in our training requirements matrix.

Do I need a license for radiography in Manitoba?

For gamma radiography, yes. The CNSC licenses the company and certifies individual exposure device operators. X-ray work falls under Manitoba's workplace safety and health rules. RT method training is needed as well as these credentials. For work in North Dakota or Minnesota, those states' radiation programmes and US radiographer certification rules apply.

What does NDT training cost in Winnipeg?

We quote on request. The price depends on the method, the level, the group size, and whether delivery is online or onsite. Send your requirements and we will return a quote within one business day. Get a Winnipeg NDT training quote.

Can Atlantis train our production welders' inspectors onsite?

Yes. We regularly design onsite programmes for manufacturers. Practicals use your equipment and specimens cut from your own product, and exams are scheduled around production.

Does Atlantis offer NAS 410, CGSB or ISO 9712 training?

No. Atlantis training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based only. Winnipeg employers also ask for NAS 410, EN 4179, CAN/CGSB-48.9712, ISO 9712 and CSWIP, and those come through other programmes and bodies.

Which method should a new technician in Winnipeg start with?

For manufacturing and fabrication, VT, MT and PT at Level I are the usual start, followed by UT. PAUT and TOFD suit pipeline and hydro work. For earnings context, see our NDT salary guide.

How can I prepare for UT Level II exams?

Work through our UT Level 2 practice questions, practise calibration in the Practical NDT simulator, and log supervised hands-on hours. The practical exam uses real specimens.

We don't employ a Level III. Can Atlantis help?

Yes. We provide outside ASNT Level III services: written practices, procedures, exam administration and certification sign-off under your written practice. See written practice development or browse the training catalogue.
